ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Apart from the reaction arrow/curved arrows, the main body in the figure is a bicyclic skeleton in which a cyclohexane is fused with a cyclopentanone on the right; the upper bridgehead carbon is connected to a methyl shown by a solid wedge, the right five-membered ring has a ketone carbonyl, and the lower bridgehead carbon is connected to a hydroxyl shown by a solid wedge. On the left side of the bicycle there is an exocyclic/exo-ring-connected iminium fragment; the nitrogen bears a positive charge and belongs to a five-membered pyrrolidine ring. One chiral carbon of the pyrrolidine ring is connected by a dashed bond to the carboxylate group CO2−. An independent H2O: is also drawn on the left, and the problem asks to ignore arrows. Reasoning: When encoding according to the molecular graph, the fused cyclohexane-cyclopentanone core retains the bridgehead stereochemistry, methyl, hydroxyl, and ketone carbonyl; the left exocyclic double bond is written as an iminium fragment formed with the positively charged pyrrolidine nitrogen, and slash/backslash is used to record the double-bond configuration; the pyrrolidine chiral carbon connects to the carboxylate C(=O)[O-]; the independent water molecule is appended with a dot as .O. Therefore the complete SMILES is C[C@]12CC/C(=[N+]3\CCC[C@H]3C(=O)[O-])C[C@@]1(O)CCC2=O.O.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image? Ignore the arrows.

method.method_draft: First visually transcribe the image into a labeled molecular graph, explicitly discarding all arrows. Start from the methyl-substituted fused bicyclic core and assign ring closures to reproduce the cyclohexane fused to the cyclopentanone. Add the stereochemical methyl-bearing bridgehead, the stereochemical hydroxyl-bearing carbon, and the ketone carbonyl. Next attach the exocyclic iminium group to the left alkene carbon, encode the positively charged pyrrolidine nitrogen and close the five-membered pyrrolidine ring. Add the chiral pyrrolidine carbon bearing the carboxylate group, with the carboxylate written as C(=O)[O-]. Finally append the separate water molecule using dot notation. Converting this complete graph with stereochemistry and charges gives the target SMILES: C[C@]12CC/C(=[N+]3\CCC[C@H]3C(=O)[O-])C[C@@]1(O)CCC2=O.O
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中除反应箭头/弯箭头外，主体是一个环己烷与右侧环戊酮稠合的双环骨架；上方桥头碳连有实楔表示的甲基，右侧五元环上有酮羰基，下方桥头碳连有实楔表示的羟基。双环左侧有一个外消旋/外环连接的亚胺鎓片段，氮带正电并属于一个五元吡咯烷环。吡咯烷环的一个手性碳以虚线键连到羧酸盐基团 CO2−。左侧还画有独立的 H2O:，题目要求忽略箭头。推理：按分子图编码时，稠合环己烷-环戊酮核心保留桥头立体化学、甲基、羟基和酮羰基；左侧外环双键写作与带正电的吡咯烷氮形成的 iminium 片段，并用斜杠/反斜杠记录双键构型；吡咯烷手性碳连接羧酸盐 C(=O)[O-]；独立水分子用点号附加为 .O。因此完整 SMILES 为 C[C@]12CC/C(=[N+]3\CCC[C@H]3C(=O)[O-])C[C@@]1(O)CCC2=O.O。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct structural transcription is the natural and essentially unique route for this image-to-SMILES task; it relies on reading the molecular graph and stereochemical wedges from the drawing rather than using reaction arrows or mechanism information.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the full molecular drawing: ignore the curved arrows, keep the separate H2O molecule, identify the fused cyclohexane/cyclopentanone skeleton with a top methyl wedge, bottom OH wedge, ketone on the five-membered ring, an exocyclic C=N+ bond to a pyrrolidine ring, and the carboxylate substituent on the pyrrolidine stereocenter with its dashed bond orientation.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt only to determine that the requested output is the SMILES for the shown transition-state structure and that arrows must be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply standard SMILES construction rules: encode ring closures for the fused bicyclic framework, use / and \ for the depicted iminium double-bond geometry, use [N+] and [O-] for formal charges, encode stereocenters with @/@@ according to the drawn wedges/dashes, and append disconnected water with dot notation.
